name: Set & Burn
subtitle: Interval timer for rounds and sets
summary: Set your work and rest, then follow the signals and voice through rounds and sets

hero.hook: Set your work and rest, then follow the signals and voice through rounds and sets
hero.shotAlt: The Set & Burn workout screen. The segment name and time left show in large numbers, with the round number and total time left below. The black ink has fallen in step with the time left.

sections.title: One workout, your shape
body: Set the work time and rounds, then shape the workout with three switches: Rest, Sets and Count jumps. You can add a warm-up and a cooldown too. The total time and the order of segments show at the top of the edit screen. Changes go into the workout only when you tap Save at the top, and Cancel leaves it as it was.

sections.title: It counts your jumps
body: With Count jumps on, the motion of your AirPods or iPhone counts jump rope jumps and running steps, and shows both as jumps. The app chooses which one to count with. Set the end rule to a count, and a round ends only when you reach its number.

sections.title: Without watching the screen
body: Each change between work and rest comes with a signal sound and a voice cue, and rounds and sets are counted for you. The 13 signal sounds are built into the app, and voice cues are read by the iOS voice on your device. The clock keeps going with the screen off. Music you are listening to keeps playing alongside.
bullets: Segment signals and voice cues

Plays alongside your music

sections.title: Segments you can read from afar
body: The screen inverts during work and returns to normal during rest. With Ink level on, the ink falls from the top with the time left during work and rest. Light and dark appearance, portrait and landscape are supported. Time in work segments adds up in Lifetime work time.

pro.title:
Make more workouts and chain them,
turn ads off
items: No limit on workouts (1 to begin with)
Workout chains that run several workouts in a row
Banner ads off on the finish screen and workout list

a: Tap the workout name at the top left of the main screen to open the workout list, then tap New workout to open the editor. Tap Save at the top to add it to the list, or Cancel to leave it out. To change the current workout's values, tap Edit on the main screen and keep the changes with Save. If you tap Cancel after changing something, the app asks once whether to discard the changes.
To begin with you can keep 1 workout, including the example. Making more takes Pro. Workouts you already have can still be used and edited.

With Pro you can join several workouts into a chain and run them in a row. In the workout list, tap New chain under Chains, add workouts, set Rest between workouts, then tap Save. A chain holds 2 to 12 workouts, and the same workout can go in twice. Rest between workouts starts at 1 minute, and at 0 the next workout follows straight away.

Choose a chain and start it, and the workouts run in the order you added them. From the second workout on, Get ready is skipped. A chain points to your workouts instead of copying them, so when you edit a workout, every chain that holds it runs with the new values. Rest between workouts is not added to Lifetime work time.

In the workout editor, turn on Count jumps and set the end rule to time or count. The first time you start a workout with Count jumps on, the app asks once for Motion & Fitness permission for AirPods motion. If you don't allow it, the iPhone's motion is used.

When motion comes in from your AirPods, they do the counting. If it stops, counting moves to the iPhone. One line on the screen shows which is counting. Earphones that don't send motion can't count. Jump rope jumps and running steps both show as jumps.

faq.q: With the screen off, or when a call comes in
a: While the timer runs, the clock, signals and voice cues continue with the screen off. If a call or alarm comes in, the timer pauses and one line shows why. Tap Resume to go on.

A set of 13 marimba signal sounds is built into the app, made with ElevenLabs. They play when work starts, when rest starts, in the last 3 seconds and at the finish. To turn them off, switch off Signal sound in Settings.

Voice cues are read only in the screen's language: English for an English screen, Korean for a Korean screen. They are read by the iOS voice on your device, not a recording, so they need no connection, and the voice and its quality differ by device. The app uses the highest-quality voice downloaded on the device. If no enhanced voice is installed, an (i) appears next to Voice in Settings and shows where to get one. To turn voice cues off, switch off Voice in Settings.
Only time in work segments is added. Rest is not counted, and there are no records by date. Clear lifetime total at the bottom of Settings sets it back to 0.

Buy it from Pro in the bar at the top of Settings. You pay once, and it is not a subscription. Pro removes the workout limit, lets you make workout chains, and turns ads off. Family Sharing is supported.
If you change devices or reinstall the app, tap Restore purchase on the Pro screen. With the same Apple Account you won't pay again.
Ads appear in two banner spots: the finish screen after a workout and the workout list. They do not appear while the timer runs.
If you see an ad that's inappropriate or unsuitable for the app's age rating, email kvndh36@naver.com with when it appeared and what it showed. The developer will review it and block it in AdMob.

iOS asks whether to allow tracking after the first-run guide closes. It does not ask if you have bought Pro. You can use the app the same way if you don't allow it, and you can change this choice in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.

Where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland, the consent form appears before the tracking prompt. In those places you can change your consent from Ad privacy choices at the bottom of Settings or the Pro screen.
The timer, Count jumps and voice cues work without a connection. Ads, buying Pro and restoring it need a connection.

iPhone with iOS 26 or later. The app's screens are in English and Korean. It uses whichever of the two comes first in your device's language list, or English if neither is there. For example, a device set to Japanese only shows English, and one with Japanese and then Korean shows Korean. There is no language setting in the app. It follows the language order in iOS Settings. Voice cues are read in the same language as the screen.
Close the app fully, open it again, and check the App Store for the latest version. If the problem continues, email us with the screen you were on and what you were doing.

privacy.title: Set & Burn Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: The developer does not collect personal information. Banner ads come from Google AdMob, which processes device information such as the advertising identifier. Motion values are used to count jumps, and the developer does not receive them. Apple handles payment for Pro.
intro: kvndh ("the developer") handles the personal information of people who use the Set & Burn app ("the app") under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act, as set out below.

sections.title: Purpose of processing
paragraphs: The app has no sign-up or login, and the developer does not collect personal information from users.
The app shows banner ads on the finish screen and in the workout list. Google's ad service AdMob selects and displays those ads, and uses device information to show ads and measure how they perform.
While a workout with Count jumps on is running, the app counts jumps and steps from the motion values of your AirPods or iPhone. This happens on your device.

sections.title: Information processed
paragraphs: The developer collects no personal information. The data the app uses is listed below. All of it is kept in the app's storage on your device, and the developer does not receive it. The app does not receive contacts, location, photos, heart rate or Health app data.
Information that AdMob may collect when showing ads is listed in section 9.
bullets: The workout list (names, times, rounds, sets, switches, end rule, counts) and the chosen workout: used to run the timer and when the app reopens
Workout chains (names, the workouts in them and their order, rest between workouts) and the chosen chain: used to run several workouts in a row
Sound, voice cue, vibration and display settings: used for how the app behaves
Lifetime work time: a single sum of seconds in work segments, with no records by date
Whether the first-run guide has been seen: used to show it only once
A copy of a save file that could not be read: the same kinds of data as above, kept when a save file is damaged

sections.title: Processing and retention period
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal information. Data in the app's storage is deleted when you delete the app. Workouts and chains can be removed in the app, and Clear lifetime total in Settings sets lifetime work time back to 0.
Information collected by AdMob is kept as set out in Google's Privacy Policy (policies.google.com/privacy).

sections.title: Disclosure to third parties
paragraphs: The developer does not provide users' personal information to third parties. However, unless you have Pro, the Google Mobile Ads SDK and Google User Messaging Platform SDK built into the app send the information in section 9 directly to Google, as follows.
bullets: Recipient: Google LLC (United States), AdMob
Purpose: checking ad consent, showing ads and measuring ad performance
Information: the device information and ad interaction records listed in section 9
When and how: sent over the internet when consent is checked and the SDK starts, and when an ad is loaded and shown
Retention: as set out in Google's Privacy Policy

Level of protection: Google complies with applicable data protection law under the Google Ads Controller-Controller Data Protection Terms. The developer lets information go only to third parties that provide the same or equal protection as this policy

sections.title: Outsourcing of processing
paragraphs: The developer does not outsource the processing of personal information. Apple processes payment for Pro and restoring it through the App Store, and payment information is governed by Apple's privacy policy. The developer does not receive your payment method or Apple Account details.

sections.title: Destruction of information
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal information, so there is nothing to destroy. Workouts and chains can be removed in the app, and deleting the app removes all of its data.

sections.title: Rights of users and legal guardians, and how to exercise them
paragraphs: Because the developer holds no personal information, there is nothing to access, correct, or delete. If you have questions, email us at the address below.

You can ask Google to give you access to, or delete, information collected by AdMob (policies.google.com/privacy). To refuse use of the advertising identifier, follow section 9. Payment information is held by Apple and is covered by Apple's privacy policy (apple.com/legal/privacy).

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: What the app uses sits as files in the app's storage on your device. The developer runs no server, and the app does not use iCloud sync. These files can be included in iCloud or Mac backups you turn on.

Motion values are received only while a workout with Count jumps on is running, including warm-up and rest, and receiving stops when it is paused or ends. AirPods motion is received only if you allow Motion & Fitness. iPhone motion is a value iOS does not ask permission for. The app asks for two permissions, Motion & Fitness and tracking (ATT). It does not ask for location, camera, microphone, photos, contacts, notifications or Health.

While a Count jumps workout is running or paused, the proximity sensor is on to prevent screen touches in a pocket, and its values are not stored. To choose the counting message, the app reads the kind of audio output in use, and this is not stored either.

sections.title: Automatic collection and how to refuse it
paragraphs: The app does not use cookies or analytics tools. It includes the Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob) and the Google User Messaging Platform SDK for advertising, which may collect the information below when they check ad consent and when they load and show ads.

After the first-run guide closes, or after the first screen appears if you have already seen it, the app checks whether you have Pro. If not, it checks ad consent information. Where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland, Google's consent form appears first. If ads can be requested and you haven't answered yet, iOS shows the App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompt. These prompts are not shown while the timer is running or paused. If you don't allow tracking, AdMob does not get the advertising identifier (IDFA), and ads keep appearing. You can change this choice in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.

If the consent result means ads can't be requested, the tracking prompt is not shown and ads are not requested. Where consent is required, change it from Ad privacy choices at the bottom of Settings or the Pro screen.
If you buy Pro, ads stop appearing, and from the next launch the app does not start the ad SDK, so the consent form and tracking prompt do not appear.
bullets: Device identifiers, and the advertising identifier (IDFA) if you allow tracking
Approximate location estimated from the IP address

sections.title: Privacy officer
paragraphs: If you have questions about personal information, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Remedies for privacy concerns
paragraphs: If you need advice about a privacy concern or help settling a dispute, you can contact the Korean bodies listed below. If you live outside Korea, you can also contact the data protection authority in your country.
bullets: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: 1833-6972 in Korea (www.kopico.go.kr)
Personal Information Infringement Report Center: 118 in Korea (privacy.kisa.or.kr)
Supreme Prosecutors' Office: 1301 in Korea (www.spo.go.kr)
National Police Agency: 182 in Korea (ecrm.police.go.kr)
European Union and EEA: the data protection authority of your country (edpb.europa.eu)
United Kingdom: Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk)
United States: Federal Trade Commission (reportfraud.ftc.gov)
Other countries: the data protection or consumer protection authority where you live
